body: - A driver call is checked by `escher_driver::validate` — a session-level one (`start` · `status` · `stop`) or the tool-level `help` by `validate_session` — before anything runs: a closed verb table of fifteen verbs in three levels (`screenshot`, the seventh asked of the held instance, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, `lint`, the eighth, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint: no argument, one result field `findings`, running no step, and `graph`, the ninth, since 2026-11-07-ui-graph: no argument, any argument refused `malformed` with nothing run, result fields `nodes` and `states`, running no step — a ratified boundary widening onto every ratified carrier, and `actions`, the tenth, since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here: no argument, any argument refused `malformed` with nothing run, one result field `nodes`, running no step — a ratified boundary widening onto every ratified carrier, and `layout`, the eleventh, since 2026-11-17-layout-on-the-carriers: one required id, refused `malformed` without it or with a second argument and `not-found` or `stale` for an unknown id, changing nothing, delivered Timer ticks left unapplied, answering the element's placement, shifts and sizes as ids, closed words and numbers), seven argument kinds with bounds (`part`, the seventh since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts, `snapshot`'s one optional argument, a whole number from 1 to 1000, `MAX_PART`), one fixed refusal order, no panic path on what a call supplies, and no `Session` in its signature — so a refused call changes nothing. A refusal is one of eight causes with fixed texts (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18; `fonts-unavailable` since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) and holds nothing of the call; a reach error is likewise one of a closed set (unknown state, refused at a step with the step's index and its closed refusal cause, or not settled at a step with the busy reading), each a fixed text holding nothing a caller supplied; keep it that way (no id, name, value or call-supplied argument name in a `Refusal`, a `Fault`, a test name or an assertion message). A fixture state name is compared whole against the app's closed table of named states before any session starts; any other name is refused as an unknown state and nothing is booted. The schema is executed by `escher_driver::Session::run`, which validates first, and since 2026-10-10-driver-cli it is reached from outside the process by three surfaces, each through `validate` before anything is sent or run: the socket's `call` request, which a host runs through `Session::run` and nothing else, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface an MCP `tools/call`, whose arguments of the wrong JSON kind are refused `malformed` before the server runs it through `Session::run` (session verbs through `validate_session`), and the `escher-session` command line (`escher_driver::command_line`) — a closed argv reader whose usage line, refusals and session errors write back nothing the caller typed, and whose stdout is the command's answer (ids, names, values and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a shot's base64 PNG and a lint's findings by the ratified crossing), never a log line; an acting driver command waits on a load in flight for at most `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time, re-settling every 10 ms, moving no time on the held instance, then `settled: false` with its busy class; since 2026-10-20-load-wait), and `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint`, `graph` and `actions` wait on none; the session's layout read, in process or through the `layout` verb on any ratified carrier, resolves its id through the run path's id resolution (refusing `stale` or `not-found`), runs no step, pump, tick or settle, and answers stable id strings, closed words and numbers, never a `NodeId`, text or value. After `validate` the executor refuses with nothing run and the instance unchanged — an id the screen does not read as `stale` or `not-found`, a `click` or a `type` on a target that cannot take it as `disabled`, `off-screen` or `covered`, in that order; a `screenshot` of an app with no font it can paint text with as `fonts-unavailable` before anything is painted, and a `lint` of one before anything is read, and one whose crop to the visible part of its element's bounds holds no pixel as `off-screen`, every refused shot leaving the instance unchanged. The session keeps a record of id text to tell `stale` from `not-found` (at most 4096 ids, none longer than `MAX_ID_BYTES`, session-lived, private): never a `NodeId` in it, never print, log or field it. Since 2026-10-19-visual-lint `Session::lint` also feeds it from its own snapshot, and `Session::actions` with every id it reads; it takes no argument and returns `Finding`s holding ids, closed defect words and numbers only (no `NodeId`, page text, colour or control value) and crosses as the `lint` verb's answer (`Command::Lint` → `Outcome::Linted`, written `{"findings":[…]}`) on every ratified carrier — the socket's `call`, the command line, MCP and a kept check, kept whole — a ratified boundary widening, with no log site, print, span or field carrying a finding and `VERBS` holding fifteen. An `Outcome` holds ids, names and values and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a shot's PNG bytes (`Outcome::Shot`) and a lint's findings (`Outcome::Linted { findings }`: stable ids, closed defect words and numbers only) and a screen's part (`Outcome::Part { text, part, parts }`, the snapshot text's own lines, written `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}`) and a UI graph (`Outcome::Graphed { graph: UiGraph }`, written `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}`, its node ids also feeding the session's record of ids) and an actions answer (`Outcome::Actions { nodes }`, written `{"nodes":[…]}`: ids, owner ids, `keyed` booleans, verb words and closed cause words) and, on an acting verb's answer (`click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`) only when the step caused something, `caused` on every ratified carrier: one item per panic, boundary error and kept record, holding its message (what its author wrote, no mask applying), location, boundary, cause chain and fields, its `error` field as its author wrote it within the text bound, every other content-named field read as redacted (a boundary widening to the error text, ratified), prints them under `Debug` and is written as JSON by `to_json` alone — as a command's answer, or as an MCP tool result's text — never log or field one; a handler `Err` the app's root error boundary takes crosses as screen content, through Dioxus's default boundary rendering of its Display, and in `caused` as one error item holding its message and cause chain under the root boundary. The driver's log records are two spans: the command span of `Session::run` (`escher_driver` / `command`), eight fields of fixed schema words, bools and counts, of a refusal its cause's name only, and since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the `tool_call` span of an MCP tool call, its parent, holding `tool` and `ending` only, both closed words (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-10) — add no field that holds what a call supplied or a screen reads — the screen text or its length, a part's number or the part count, a shot's image, its size or its dimensions, a lint's findings or their count included a graph's ids, component, state and handler event names and an actions answer's ids, owner ids, verb words and causes a layout answer and a step's caused text, from a driver call or an in-process read, included (a `screenshot`, a `lint`, an `actions` call or a part read records `verb` and, refused, `cause`; a `graph` or a `layout` call records `verb` and, refused, `cause`).

body:
Added layout, the fifteenth driver verb, at the instance level after actions: it takes one required id and answers why that element sits where it does at its size, using only ids, closed words and numbers. The verb changes nothing.
The layout answer now crosses every ratified carrier: the session socket call, the command line, the MCP tool (after actions, with help last) and a kept check at rest that replay compares. Before this session the layout read was in process only.
Driver verbs went from 14 to 15, instance verbs from 10 to 11, MCP tools from 14 to 15 and the per-node verbs in the actions answer from 4 to 5, with layout last and no cause. The Cells actions answer at boot was measured at 118,292 bytes, up from 106,088.
An element the snapshot lists but the engine cannot explain now answers the new unexplained placer at its snapshot bounds. Each JSON writer has a fallback word for later engine set members, so there is no panic path.
Exploration still covers only click, type and scroll, now chosen by field kind, so verbs whose results hold an image or a layout reading are left out. The cold-agent pipe's verb list stays at fourteen (founder fork F1, provisional).
No new IPC method, socket, environment variable, crate, dependency, refusal cause, session error, exit status, node key or span field was added.

body_fields.fact: The layout answer crosses every ratified carrier (the session socket, the command line, MCP and a kept check at rest). It holds only stable ids, closed kebab-case words and numbers, and no text, attribute or name.

The layout verb is an instance verb with one required id argument. It changes nothing in the session and leaves delivered Timer ticks unapplied. It answers not-found or stale for an unknown id, and malformed without an id or with a second argument.

The layout answer's words are closed sets. The placing words are block, flex, grid, table, inline, float, absolute, fixed, root, select, select-list, unexplained and app. The shift words are scroll and transform. The cause words are style, min, max, flex-grow, flex-shrink, stretch, grid, table, replaced, content and layout. A later engine member writes a fallback word, never a panic.
An element the snapshot lists that the engine cannot explain answers the unexplained placer at its snapshot bounds, not an engine placer.
A kept check holds a layout step and its whole answer, and replay stops on a changed placed value.
Exploration covers only target verbs whose results hold no image and no layout reading, by field kind, so layout is never explored.
As a provisional exception (founder fork F1), the cold-agent pipe keeps its verb list at fourteen without layout. Until the founder decides, a live run reads not-isolated.
